title: PostgreSQL DSN handling
description: The Stack section names SQLite as the backend. The Database section also accepts a PostgreSQL DSN. Only SQLite is graded.

options.label: SQLite is graded. A postgres DSN is passed to the shipped library unchanged, with no PostgreSQL acceptance check.
Add a PostgreSQL acceptance check to the Blueprint.

title: Sea Trial IDs st-010 and st-011 are absent
description: ANALYSIS.md names st-010 and st-011 as added guardrails, but SEA_TRIALS.md defines only st-001 through st-009.
system_choice: Trace only st-001 through st-009. No story accepts st-010 or st-011, and no ID is invented.

title: Concurrent processes
description: The sources define per-command atomicity only. AC-009 requires two concurrent processes to each run as one transaction.
system_choice: Rely on the database's own transaction isolation. Add no application-level locking.

title: First-run and empty-data behavior
description: The sources do not state what happens before init, or what reports show on empty tables.
system_choice: A missing SQLite file is created empty by the first command. A command that finds no tables exits 1 with nothing on stdout. Reports on empty tables write the header and a zero TOTAL row.

title: Launcher logging and packaging
description: Launchers use plain POSIX sh without the common.md tee log capture, because POSIX sh lacks pipefail and tee would mask the test exit status. pyproject.toml sets [tool.uv] package = false, since ledger is an application and not an installable wheel. Is that acceptable, or should logging be added on replan?

title: How atomicity is achieved over the shipped Database
description: The shipped persistence/db.py commits inside every create, update and delete, so wrapping the command alone cannot roll back an earlier write. I shadowed driver.connect for the duration of one command with a proxy that makes commit() a no-op, forwards everything else, and commits once after the command returns (or rolls back on any exception). The shadow is removed in a finally block. This needed no change to the shipped persistence files. Alternatives were editing db.py (forbidden: it is a Drydock-shipped file) or adding a transaction primitive to DATABASE.md (outside this step). Is this acceptable, or should it change on replan?

title: Module location versus ARCHITECTURE.md
description: The spec places run_command in cli.transactional, but ARCHITECTURE.md says cli/ has no DB access. I followed the spec and kept the module under cli/. It touches only the persistence handle, not a driver, so the import boundary holds.

title: Leading zeros in the integer part
description: The pattern -?DIGITS[.D[D]] allows any run of digits, so '007' parses to 700 and '00.5' parses to 50. I kept this rather than rejecting leading zeros, because the spec only forbids zero values and excess decimals. Say if leading zeros should be rejected instead.

title: Shape check before calendar check
description: check_date enforces the exact YYYY-MM-DD shape with an ASCII-digit regex before calling date.fromisoformat, because fromisoformat also accepts compact forms like 20260101. Is that acceptable?

title: Carriage return treated as a line break
description: The spec forbids only a newline. I also reject a carriage return (\r) in names and memos, since it is a line break that would corrupt line-oriented CSV and output. Is that acceptable, or should only \n be rejected?

title: Indexes derived from the persistence declaration
description: The rendered schema indexes transactions(account); transactions(category). Each is implied by the declaration — a foreign key is looked up by its child column, and a read pattern's Input fields are the predicate it filters on. Declare an `- INDEX (...)` bullet in DATABASE.md for any index this does not cover.
